Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Follow-up from our security/compliance team: we
need a short note outlining how Redwood Private (VPC) would handle cross-border failover
for a deployment where primary workloads sit in the EU and secondary warm-standby sits in
APAC. Key asks:
- Proof we can guarantee EU data-at-rest and control-plane anchors remain in EU under
  normal ops.
- Network patterns used for replication (VPC peering, VPN, Transit Gateway) and the
  minimum egress footprint.
- How KV cache and token metadata are treated during failover to avoid data leakage.
- Expected RTO / RPO for model serving, and what the observable signals are.

I've attached our residency checklist and a draft network diagram for the target topology.
Can you confirm whether the architecture requires any vendor network peering in-country
or if we can use transit through our cloud provider's backbone? Also, we have a narrow
procurement window — would appreciate a one-page summary we can circulate to our InfoSec
board.

Thanks,

Sophie — thanks for the clear list and the diagram. Looping in Rishi (runtime/networking) and
Lauren (commercial/security tie-offs). We'll produce: 1) a one-page summary for your InfoSec
board, and 2) a technical note describing the replication and failover behavior with RTO/RPO
estimates. Quick answers up front:

- Control plane and customer-managed KMS: can be anchored to the EU. Customer can opt to
  run the control plane in their EU VPC or Redwood-managed EU tenancy; both options keep
  control-plane metadata in the EU under normal operations.
- Cross-region replication for model servers uses one of two patterns: encrypted VPC-to-VPC
  peering (private link) when low hop-count is required, or a configuration that uses the
  cloud provider transit gateway with strict route filters to minimize egress. Both options
  encrypt traffic end-to-end and avoid public internet.
- KV cache and ephemeral runtime state: by default caches are local to the serving cluster.
  We replicate only the minimal control metadata needed for session continuity (session
  token IDs and checkpoint pointers), never customer prompt or content payloads, unless
  explicitly configured for cross-region warm-standby.

Rishi — can you draft the short technical note (bullet points + expected timings) and a
suggested small diagram that highlights our recommended pattern for Acme? Sophie — any
sensitivity thresholds we should know about (e.g., absolute ban on any token metadata
leaving EU)?

Neha / Sophie / team — quick technical note below. I'll attach a 1-page diagram to the
Hub link.

Summary (short bullets for InfoSec):
- Design: Primary model-serving clusters in EU (region eu-west-1). Warm-standby cluster in
  APAC (ap-northeast-1). Control-plane endpoints remain in EU. Cross-region links use
  cloud provider Transit Gateway peering with static routes and ACLs.
- Data-at-rest: customer datasets and S3 buckets are pinned to EU storage. Model weights
  are replicated via encrypted object replication only when customer authorizes warm-standby.
- KV / cache policy: runtime caches are ephemeral and local. We replicate only sequence
  pointers and a minimal session manifest (no prompt payloads). Session manifests are
  encrypted with keys anchored to the EU KMS; only lookup tokens (opaque IDs) move across
  regions.
- Failover behavior: automatic failover is off by default. We recommend a manual-orchestrated
  cutover for cross-border failover to satisfy compliance review. Steps: 1) validate control
  plane anchor, 2) snapshot cache manifests, 3) promote APAC cluster to primary (DNS switchover
  + route update), 4) rehydrate caches from encrypted snapshots. Typical RTO: 6-12 minutes for
  cold start rehydration; RPO: last checkpointed manifest (~30s-5m depending on checkpointing
  frequency).
- Observable signals: continuous heartbeat on control plane, replication lag > 30s, and
  cache-consistency checksum mismatch trigger alerts and automatic rollback options.

Notes / mitigations:
- To avoid in-flight prompt exposure, we recommend the application fronting traffic to a
  regional ingress that terminates TLS inside the customer's EU VPC with private peering to
  Redwood runtime.
- If Acme requires absolute prohibition of any metadata leaving EU, we can support a fully
  EU-only standby pattern using cold snapshots shipped via encrypted object copy and manual
  restore (longer RTO).

Attachments: network-failover-patterns-v1.pdf (uploaded to shared drive)

Happy to iterate. If you want, Marissa and I can run a tabletop test with your infra team
(next week).

- Rishi
